source: EPA AP-42, Fifth Edition, Volume I, Chapter 2: Solid Waste Disposal; IPCC AR6 WGIII
note: Emissions factors represent kg CO2e AVOIDED per kg of material recycled (vs landfilling/incineration). Used for carbon credit calculation: CO2e avoided (tonnes) = waste_weight_kg × factor (kg CO2e/kg) ÷ 1000.
unit: kg CO2e avoided per kg material

aluminum.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
aluminum.notes: Aluminum recycling avoids ~95% of virgin production emissions

steel_cans.notes: Steel/tin can recycling avoids ~60-70% of virgin production emissions

pet_plastic.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
pet_plastic.notes: PET bottle recycling avoids ~70% of virgin production emissions

hdpe_plastic.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
hdpe_plastic.notes: HDPE recycling avoids ~65% of virgin production emissions

glass.notes: Glass recycling avoids ~30% of virgin production emissions

paper_cardboard.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
paper_cardboard.notes: Paper recycling avoids ~40% of virgin production emissions; avoids methane from landfill

organic_compost.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
organic_compost.notes: Composting avoids methane emissions from anaerobic landfill decomposition

e_waste.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
e_waste.notes: E-waste recycling recovers metals and avoids hazardous landfill leaching

tires.notes: Tire recycling avoids methane and avoids virgin rubber production

general_mixed_recyclables.source: EPA AP-42 Ch.2; IPCC AR6 WGIII
general_mixed_recyclables.notes: Conservative estimate for mixed recyclable waste

credit_conversion: 1 carbon credit = 1 tonne CO2e avoided (rounded down)
demo_note: For hackathon demo only. Values are estimates for demonstration purposes.
